enhancement.text: 1-ID uses X-rays at about 40 to 140 keV to measure stress and crystal grains through centimetres of metal. A keV is a thousand electron-volts. The upgrade plan replaces the bent-silicon-crystal monochromator, which selects one X-ray energy, with a horizontally deflecting version. This avoids blurring the smaller vertical source and adds a sample-handling and detector system at 1-ID-C. In 2026, the 1-ID-C system has been delivered and 1-ID-E retains its old setup. Installation of the new monochromator and planned superconducting undulator is not confirmed.
fdrDeliverables: 1-ID-C: sample manipulation system with hexapod and tilt stage

enhancement.text: 2-ID scans small X-ray spots across samples to map elements. Each element emits fluorescence at characteristic energies. The plan adds a mirror to each branch to image the source onto a fixed aperture, reducing sensitivity to the 2.5-fold vertical source-size change between operating modes. It replaces 2-ID-E zone plates with Kirkpatrick–Baez mirrors, raising transmission from 10 to 20% to 60 to 80%, and builds Bionanoprobe-II for frozen samples with a 10 nm resolution goal. In 2026, Bionanoprobe-II is under construction and 2-ID-E still uses zone plates.

enhancement.text: 3-ID selects X-rays within about 0.001 eV out of 14,400 eV, better than one part in ten million. These excite nuclei of selected isotopes, including iron-57, to measure atomic vibrations in enzymes or samples under pressure. New Kirkpatrick–Baez focusing mirrors reduce the spot from about 20 µm toward 1 µm for diamond-anvil cells. In 2026, the iron-57 monochromator provides a 1.5 × 12 µm horizontal × vertical spot. A planned cryogenic monochromator depends on funding, and installation is not confirmed.

SEES (May 2025): 57Fe NRIXS/NFS available with a 1.5 x 12 um (H x V) focus; ~10 x 10 um planned for Kr/Eu/Dy. An energy-domain Mossbauer spectrometer was under development for late 2025. Undulators installed are 2.7 cm (not the FDR 2.5 cm).

enhancement.text: 7-ID measures rapid changes by starting a reaction with a laser pulse and probing it after a controlled delay with an X-ray pulse. The enhancement is delivered, and the general user program has fully resumed in 2026.
